verdict.rationale: Codex documents a skill creator that interviews the user about what a skill does, when it triggers, and whether it needs scripts. A recorder drafts reusable skills from demonstrations, and the built-in @plugin-creator skill scaffolds the plugin manifest and a local marketplace entry for packaging. A community user confirms building proprietary skills with the skill-creator skill, and a probe confirmed plugin-creator installs as a real skill. Missing for 10: a documented meta-skill capability for improving or iterating on existing skills, and in-depth first-party docs on the skill-creator workflow beyond a single line.

support.subject: As a developer, the collection ships a meta-skill or tool that guides my agent through writing, improving, and packaging new skills

citations.quote: The creator asks what the skill does, when it should trigger, and whether it should stay instruction-only or include scripts.
The recorder captures the workflow, inspects the steps, and drafts a reusable skill from the demonstration.
For the fastest setup, use the built-in `@plugin-creator` skill. It scaffolds the required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifest and can also generate a local marketplace entry for testing.
The skills that matter most to this user are ones they build themselves with the skill-creator skill for proprietary workflows
